# 1 Enoch Chapter 60 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** In the year five hundred, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month — during Enoch's lifetime — I saw in this parable how a tremendous earthquake made the heaven of heavens tremble, and the whole host of the Most High, all the angels, millions upon millions, were convulsed with violent agitation.

**2** The Head of Days sat on his throne of glory, with angels and the righteous standing in attendance around him.

**3** A terrible trembling seized me. Fear had me in its grip, my legs gave out, my strength drained away, and I fell face-down.

**4** Michael sent one of the holy angels who lifted me up. When he raised me, my spirit returned to me — I had simply not been able to bear the sight of that host, or the uproar and the quaking of heaven.

**5** Michael said to me: "Why are you so terrified by this vision? Today is still the day of his mercy — he has been compassionate and patient with all who live on earth.

**6** But when the day arrives — the day of his power, his punishment, his judgment — the day the Lord of Spirits has set aside for those who refuse to honor the righteous law, who deny righteous judgment, who use his name as a hollow word — on that day a covenant awaits the elect, but sinners face a full inquisition."

**7** On that same day, two great creatures were separated from one another: a female creature called Leviathan, appointed to live in the deep abyss of the ocean, over the springs of water;

**8** and a male creature called Behemoth, who settled with his chest in a vast desert waste called Duidain, east of the garden where the elect and righteous live — the same place where my grandfather was taken up to heaven, he who was seventh from Adam, the first human the Lord of Spirits ever made.

**9** I asked the other angel to show me the power of these two creatures — how they had been separated on a single day and placed, one in the depths of the sea and the other in the desert wilderness.

**10** He said to me: "You, son of man — you are seeking to know what is hidden."

**11** The other angel who traveled with me, who had been showing me hidden things, explained to me what is first and last in the heaven above, and beneath the earth in the depths, and at the far edges of heaven, and on heaven's foundations.

**12** He showed me the storerooms of the winds, and how the winds are divided and weighed, and how the wind-portals are counted — each one measured by the power of its wind; and the influence of the moon's light, and the proper order of things; and the groupings of the stars by name, and how every division is assigned.

**13** He showed me the thunders and where they strike, and all the divisions among the lightning-flashes so that they may flash out, and the armies of lightning that instantly obey their orders.

**14** Thunder has its appointed resting places, and it is given a fixed period. Though thunder and lightning are two distinct things, they are inseparable — they travel together through the spirit and never part.

**15** When the lightning flashes, the thunder voices its reply; and the spirit enforces a pause between the two, dividing the interval equally. The treasury of thunder-peals is as vast as the sand; each peal is reined in and redirected by the power of the spirit, then sent out according to the countless regions of the earth.

**16** The spirit of the sea is masculine and powerful; according to the full force of his strength he pulls it back with a rein — and then drives it forward again, scattering it across all the mountains of the earth.

**17** The spirit of the hoarfrost has its own dedicated angel; the spirit of hail is a good angel.

**18** The spirit of snow has left its chambers because of its powerful force — there is a special spirit within it, and what rises from it looks like smoke. Its name is frost.

**19** The spirit of the mist does not share chambers with the others — it has its own private chamber. Its course is splendid, in light and in darkness, in winter and in summer, and an angel dwells in its chamber.

**20** The spirit of the dew has its home at heaven's far edges, where it connects to the chambers of rain. It operates in winter and summer both; the clouds of dew and the clouds of mist are linked together, each feeding the other.

**21** When the spirit of rain departs from its chamber, the angels come, open the chamber, and lead the rain out. Once it spreads across the whole earth, it merges with the water already there.

**22** And whenever it merges with the water on the earth...

**23** For these waters are the provision for all who live on earth — nourishment for the earth, sent down from the Most High in heaven. Therefore there is a measured quota for the rain, and the angels are charged with managing it.

**24** I saw all this as I looked toward the Garden of the Righteous.

**25** The angel of peace who was with me said: "These two creatures — made in keeping with the greatness of God — shall feed..."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Ch. 60 is the most ambitious chapter in the Parables. The Leviathan/Behemoth cosmogony (vv. 7–9) expands Job 40–41, here making the two creatures gendered (female/male) and assigning them cosmic locations. The meteorological treatise (vv. 11–23) shows the Enochic tradition's interest in natural philosophy as revealed wisdom. V. 25 is fragmentary in all MSS.*
